reader_question: Which age groups report voting most and least?
title: Citizens 18 to 24 reported voting at the lowest rate of four age groups in every presidential year from 2004 to 2024.
measure_line: Share of citizens who reported voting, by age, in presidential years from 2004, the first with these age groups, to 2024, United States
notes: In every year the youngest group trails the next, citizens 25 to 44, by 11 to 16 points.
source_line: Source: U.S. Census Bureau, Current Population Survey Voting and Registration Supplement, Table A-1, reported voting, citizen voting-age population, November 1978 to 2024, United States. Retrieved November 6, 2026. Self-reported in a survey; citizenship data before 1996 are not fully comparable.
alt: Four lines of reported voting by age in presidential years from 2004 to 2024, each named beside it: 65 and over highest, near 71 to 75 percent; 45 to 64 next; 25 to 44 below; and 18 to 24 lowest, in red, from 46.7 percent in 2004 to 47.7 percent in 2024.

table.caption: Share of citizens who reported voting, by age, percent

notes_internal: Rule 14.3's correct plate. Checked by script: 18 to 24 more than 10 points below every other group in each year (gaps 11.2 to 16.1). The line the title names takes the red point (the data lead's ruling (f), RS-S4): an age group carries no tie on Rule 14.6's list.
